title: Prevent credit line drop during export when reserved capacity discounts overlap rate-limit credits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Exports to NetSuite are intermittently omitting negative invoice line items that represent a combination of reserved capacity discounts and later-applied rate-limit credits. This results in NetSuite invoices that do not match Stripe/ledger state and causes accounting reconciliation failures and incorrect customer-facing invoices for a small subset of customers who simultaneously have reserved capacity commitments and late-applied rate-limit credits or manual adjustments.

Observed behavior: The billing export pipeline aggregates line items by invoice/sku and then drops lines whose aggregated quantity and amount normalize to zero or where normalization logic considers sign ambiguous. When a reserved capacity discount (negative invoice lines) is merged with a rate-limit credit that was applied retroactively, rounding and sign normalization code paths sometimes collapse the final exportable line into a no-op and the line is not emitted to NetSuite. Additionally, export idempotency keys for those merged credit lines are sometimes generated using a transient key that differs between the original invoice export and the corrected/credit export, causing follow-up exports to be treated as new lines instead of amendments.

Why this matters: NetSuite expects explicit negative invoice lines for discounts/credits so they can be applied to invoices/credit memos. Dropping them leads to invoice amount mismatches, requires manual accounting adjustments, and trips downstream automated reconciliation alerts. The issue is most visible during mid-cycle credits and dedicated-customer reserved-capacity discounts where usage adjustments and rate-limit credits are applied after the initial invoice export.

Scope: Affects ~0.7% of invoices where: 1) customer has reserved capacity discounts active, 2) a rate-limit credit or manual credit is created against the same billing period after the initial export, and 3) the combination of discounts/credits causes small fractional rounding differences when normalized to the export currency.

Timeline: Investigation started 2026-02-22 after accounting flagged a set of mismatched invoices. Root-cause hypothesis validated with a small repro harness on 2026-02-27. Work plan created 2026-03-01.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a test org with reserved capacity (monthly commit) that produces deterministic discount negative lines on invoices.
Generate usage that triggers a rate-limit credit (simulate throttling or apply credit via internal billing API) and ensure credit is applied after initial invoice export time window.
Trigger the export pipeline (billing-export-runner) to produce Stripe->export intermediate payload, then run NetSuite mapping/merge path (export-merge-worker).
Observe that the expected negative credit line is missing from the final NetSuite export payload and NetSuite invoice net amount differs from Stripe ledger.
Compare idempotency keys between original invoice export and follow-up credit export to confirm key mismatch or normalization collapse.
proposed_solution:
1) Change export aggregation to never implicitly drop negative/credit lines: always emit explicit negative line items even when aggregated net is zero—mark as 'credit-aggregate' so NetSuite can process as adjustments.
2) Normalize rounding deterministically to account currency precision before aggregation (use banker's rounding at cents precision).
3) Make idempotency key generation include a stable origin tuple (invoice_id, adjustment_event_id, export_window_ts) so follow-up exports become proper amendments instead of new lines.
4) Update NetSuite mapping to accept and apply explicit zero-amount-adjustment lines as credits (to capture audit trail), and add guardrails so finance can reconcile automated corrections.
5) Add a backfill job to re-export affected invoices for the last 90 days and mark them with a special export tag so finance can detect amended invoices.
implementation_notes:
- Add unit tests around aggregation logic covering negative/positive/zero-edge cases and cross-currency rounding.
- Modify export schema field 'export_line_kind' allowed values: charge | credit | credit-aggregate | adjustment.
- Ensure export runner produces stable idempotency_key using (invoice_id, origin_event_id, consolidated_key_version='v2').
- Update export-merge-worker to preserve explicit negative lines and not coalesce them away.
- Add feature flag 'emit_explicit_credit_lines' behind which we can safely roll out and measure diff.
- Add monitoring: alert when export delta (Stripe amount vs NetSuite exported amount) > $0.50 for a single invoice after re-export.
- Prepare a backfill orchestrator (safe re-export) that runs in low-traffic windows and annotates exports with 'amendment' metadata.
- Coordinate with Finance to queue re-export approvals and org-level exceptions.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for aggregation and idempotency.
- Integration test that runs full export against staging NetSuite sandbox.
- Manual verification: pick 10 known affected invoices from prod window and run backfill in sandbox to verify exported lines are present.
- Smoke test: enable feature flag for 10% of exports and monitor accounting deltas over 48 hours.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Add metric billing.export.delta_amount_by_invoice and alert if > $1 for any invoice post-export.
- Pager rule: if >10 invoice mismatches detected in 24h, page oncall billing-eng.
- Dashboard panels for finance to see amendment exports and reconciliation success rate.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy aggregation changes behind flag billing.emit_explicit_credit_lines.
2) Run staging exports to NetSuite sandbox and get finance signoff.
3) Enable flag for 10% of orgs for 48h, monitor.
4) Gradually ramp to 100% over 72h if no regressions.
5) Run backfill for last 90 days in controlled batches (finance-approved).
postmortem_actions:
- Add a reconciliation test to CI that simulates reserved capacity + late credits and validates export equality.
- Update runbook for finance to handle amendment exports and how to reconcile in NetSuite.
- Retrospective with billing, finance, and platform to review export contracts and SLAs.
- Schedule quarterly review to ensure rounding rules are consistent across currency and external export targets.
